title: Orbit-style Quickstart hub illustrations and step-slice assets
creator: Asha Patel
description: Design an "Orbit" visual system for the Quickstart landing experience: a radial hero illustration and a set of modular "step-slice" diagrams that scale across breakpoint widths. Deliverables: three hero variants (static, subtle-motion Lottie, and interactive hover state), a library of 6 step-slice diagrams (single-step, progressive 3-step, 5-step roadmap, API flow slice, VIP onboarding slice, and 'try-it-now' snapshot), responsive artboards (320 / 768 / 1440), screenshot-ready component mockups for docs, and export tokens for engineering (SVG/PNG/WebP + Lottie JSON). Include accessibility contrast checks, clear microcopy for CTAs, and an export pipeline for automated screenshot capture (Percy). The visual identity should be distinct from previous 'tile/hero' iterations: aim for a radial, orbital metaphor that communicates stages circling a developer-first core. Work with content and research to make steps scannable and testable by prototype participants.
acceptance_criteria: Three hero variants uploaded to Figma with named components and usage notes
Six step-slice diagrams exported as responsive components and documented
Screenshot pipeline configured with at least two canonical pages captured by Percy
Accessibility contrast >= AA for text and icons; hero motion respects prefers-reduced-motion
Engineering has tokenized color/spacing values and a single SVG sprite for icons
Design review approved and PR merged to docs repo with screenshot fixtures
comments: 2026-02-12 - Asha P: Kickoff complete. Ran alignment with PM (Nora) and Eng (Mateo). Decided on orbital metaphor over linear ladder after stakeholder moodboard review.
2026-02-18 - Liam C: Low-fi explorations uploaded to Figma. Two directions: concentric ring + central card, and staggered orbits with step-slices. Team prefers staggered orbits for scannability.
2026-02-22 - Nora S (PM): Recommend emphasizing 'Try in 5 minutes' CTA in hero variant B. PM requests analytics event names for CTA clicks (ENG-2999 will add the tracking hook).
2026-02-25 - Design critique: Accessibility flagged - some pastel gradients fail AA on small text. Action: tighten palette and add 2 high-contrast variants.
2026-03-02 - Liam C: Mid-fi prototypes with interactive hover states and reduced-motion toggles. Shared Lottie proof-of-concept; file attached to Figma.

2026-03-04 - UX Research (Maya): Prototype tested with 6 dev participants. Key takeaway: orbit metaphor helps orient users but they want clearer step labels. Action: add numbered badges and short microcopy.
2026-03-07 - Asha P: Updated acceptance criteria to include screenshot pipeline. Shared PR to docs for screenshot fixtures (GH #638).
2026-03-10 - Eng review (Mateo R): Implementation caution: complex hover states may add JS cost on low-tier pages. Recommendation: provide non-JS fallback and defer Lottie until after roll-out.
2026-03-12 - Liam C: Final assets exported (SVG + Lottie). Preparing handoff doc and token table. Setting up Percy snapshots for hero, 3-step, and API-slice pages.
notes: Trade-offs considered: fully interactive hero (higher engagement) vs static with microinteraction (faster load). Chose progressive enhancement: static default + Lottie when bandwidth allows.
Implementation guidance included: namespaced CSS classes (.orbit-hero, .step-slice), recommended lazy-load for Lottie, and an artifacts directory structure for release engineers.
Design tokens: primary-orbit-600, accent-orbit-300, step-badge-contrast; spacing tokens follow 4px baseline and map to existing token names for easiest swap-in.
